data.title: USDA WASDE Report Sparks Liquidation Rush in Corn Futures — Update
data.description:
By Kirk Maltais

The Agriculture Department lifted its projections for the size of this year's corn crop, sparking traders to accelerate the liquidation of their sizable long holdings.

The USDA forecast corn production would be at its second-highest level ever, at 16.03 billion bushels, in the 2026/27 marketing year, behind last year's 17 billion bushels of corn produced, in its monthly World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report published Friday.

Average yields are anticipated at 181.2 bushels an acre, a 2.7 bushels-an-acre increase from the USDA's September estimate. Analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal forecast yield this month at 177.6 bushels an acre, a 0.9 bushels-an-acre decline from last month.

Most-active corn futures trading on the Chicago Board of Trade plummeted after the USDA released its updated projections, falling 5.1% to $4.89 a bushel - retreating under the $5 a bushel mark.

The larger corn crop, combined with last month's quarterly stock report showing larger-than-expected inventories of corn, has the market rethinking its assumptions about the weather stress seen in the latter-half of the summer and its effect on crop health.

"Sept. 1 stocks coming in 173 million bushels above the September WASDE pretty much guaranteed ending stocks would climb," said Brian Grete, senior grain and livestock analyst with Commstock Investments. "But not this much, because a smaller crop was anticipated."

Fund traders were largely expecting a shrinking corn crop this year, with last week's Commitment of Traders report from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission showing a net long position of 377,850 contracts among managed money. The agency will be publishing an updated version of the report later Friday afternoon.

For soybeans, the USDA affirmed its estimates for record-large production and yields for the 2026/27 crop. The USDA said 4.56 billion bushels of soybeans would be harvested in the U.S. this fall, boasting an average yield of 53.1 bushels an acre. Both figures are record-highs for U.S. soybeans, with the previous record for production set at 4.46 billion bushels in 2021 and yields at 53 bushels an acre in 2025.

Friday's move in soybeans was largely expected by analysts, but the surprise factor in corn has diverted attention away from soybeans and wheat.

"The numbers couldn't get much worse for the corn," Charlie Sernatinger, executive vice president with Marex Capital Markets, said in a note following the WASDE's release. "The beans were 'neutral,' but nothing is neutral when the grain locomotive takes off in a new direction."

Most-active soybean futures are down 0.9%, while wheat has fallen 2.6%.

Write to Kirk Maltais at kirk.maltais@wsj.com

data.title: Lakshmi Venu pushes for settlement along lines of TVS family partition
data.description:
To settle the dispute over wealth sharing within the Venu Srinivasan family, Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan and Mallika Srinivasan, is understood to be pushing for a settlement along the lines of the broader TVS family partition in 2020.

Sudarshan Venu

Sources close to Lakshmi said that the harmonious partition and settlement between four major wings of the TVS family can be a model to settle the wealth of the Venu Srinivasan group comprising of TVS Motor, Sundaram Clayton, TVS Holdings, and TVS Credit.

In 2020, the larger TVS family comprising multiple branches valued all assets, divided them on a mutually agreeable basis and also compensated family members.

However, this demand has led to an impasse.

According to insiders, Venu Srinivasan and Sudarshan have shown resistance to a formal settlement. “Multiple requests by Lakshmi Venu to her father and brother, Sudarshan, over the last several months have been met with silence,” said a person close to the family. The father-son duo is understood to be of the view that a family settlement was already executed via a 2024 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by all four members.

However, this particular MoU, reviewed by businessline, does not speak of any financial settlement and just lays down details of brand rights and non-compete arrangements.

As per the document, Venu and Sudarshan control automobiles, financial services, real estate and drone business of TVS Holdings, and Venu and Lakshmi control Sundaram-Clayton. Mallika and Lakshmi manage TAFE, which is not part of the TVS group.

The dispute started when Lakshmi came to know of a TVS Holdings statutory filing in April 2025 declaring significant beneficial ownership in favour of Sudarshan Venu.

“Lakshmi was shocked as family wealth cannot be allocated unilaterally without discussion,” the source said. She is not taking legal action yet and continues to try and address this internally, the person added.

businessline has also learnt that Mallika Srinivasan, as the mother of Lakshmi and Sudarshan, is attempting to get the family together for a dialogue and believes that it could be settled within. “She wants this issue to end with a fair and equitable settlement and is in favour of getting a neutral mediator for the purpose ​,” a close family source said, adding that there should be no gender disparity in sharing of the family wealth.

The source emphasised that the issue is not just about economic settlement between family members but about ownership and management of the group companies. “Someone who has managed the company, even if he did well, cannot claim ownership over it,” the source said.

Mallika is said to have taken a strong view that a person creating value in the company does not automatically extinguish legal ownership rights of the other.

As of Friday, TVS Holdings had a market cap of ₹23,180 crore, TVS Motor is valued at ₹1,83,621 crore and Sundaram Clayton at around ₹2,702 crore.

data.title: Canadian dollar hits 18-month low as jobs data clips rate hike bets
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar weakened to an 18-month low against its US counterpart on Friday as domestic data showed a surprise drop in employment, reducing expectations for a Bank of Canada interest rate hike this month.

The loonie was trading 0.4% lower at 1.4275 per US dollar, or 70.05 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since April 2025 at 1.4298. For the week, the currency was down 0.2%, putting it on track for its fifth straight weekly decline.

  • Canada's economy shed 68,300 jobs in September, while the unemployment rate edged up to 6.5% from 6.4% in August. Economists had forecast an increase of 9,200 jobs.

  • "A second consecutive month of sizable job losses washes away the surprising strength reported in Canada's job market through the early summer, and leaves employment up a so-so 0.5% from a year ago," Douglas Porter, chief economist at BMO Capital Markets, said in a note.

  • "We continue to believe that the appropriate stance by the Bank of Canada is watchful waiting, particularly so with employment suddenly clouding over," Porter said.

  • The BoC has said it is prepared to raise borrowing costs multiple times if inflation remained too high but it has also worried that new US tariffs had increased uncertainty around the sustainability of Canada's economic rebound.

  • Investors see a 25% chance the central bank raises its benchmark interest rate on October 28, down from 40% before the employment report. (0#CADIRPR)

  • The US dollar rose against a basket of major currencies as oil prices recovered from session lows. US crude oil futures were trading 0.3% lower at $91.19 a barrel.

  • Canadian government bond yields moved lower across the curve, with the market set to close early ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Monday.

  • The 2-year (CA2YT=RR) was down 6.8 basis points at 3.183%, falling 10.9 basis points further below the equivalent US rate to a gap of about 161 basis points, its widest since February 2025.

data.title: GreenPower Announces LOI with Invisible Urban Charging for Deploying EV Buses at Scale
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 9, 2026) - GreenPower Motor Company Inc. ("GreenPower"), a leading manufacturer and distributor of all-electric, purpose-built, zero-emission medium and heavy-duty vehicles serving the cargo and delivery market, shuttle and transit space and school bus sector, today announced they have entered into a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Invisible Urban Charging, Inc. ("IUC") to establish a framework to evaluate and jointly develop integrated electric-fleet solutions that combine GreenPower's electric vehicle platforms with IUC's charging infrastructure, software, operations and capital-solutions capabilities. IUC has secured in excess of US$2.5 billion to further the development of its electric mobility program.

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12024/318308_6935d417b448b98f_002full.jpg

The EV Star Cab & Chassis is the foundation of an LOI entered into today between GreenPower and IUC to jointly develop integrated electric-fleet solutions.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12024/318308_6935d417b448b98f_002full.jpg

Under the LOI, GreenPower and IUC intend to evaluate opportunities involving the EV Star Cab & Chassis, electric buses, shuttles, cab-and-chassis platforms, strip chassis and other commercial electric vehicles; fleet telematics and route and energy optimization; local body completion, assembly, sourcing and domestic-production pathways; maintenance, warranty, parts, training and lifecycle support; and potential project-level financing, leasing, fleet-as-a-service, charging-as-a-service and other capital solutions.

"This LOI creates a practical framework for GreenPower and IUC to evaluate how purpose-built electric vehicle platforms, charging infrastructure, software and capital solutions can be integrated for fleet customers in qualified markets. The LOI also sets out the framework where GreenPower would use bodybuilders in international markets to build locally all-electric shuttle buses utilizing GreenPower's EV Star Cab Chassis," said GreenPower CEO Fraser Atkinson. "We look forward to working with IUC to assess vehicle configurations, localization pathways and customer-ready solutions."

Added Jake Bezzant, CEO of IUC, "As our clients increasingly ask for us to cover more of the EV ecosystem, including fleet transition, teaming with GreenPower Motors gives us a partner that can deliver high-quality vehicles and support our own effort to deliver a best-in-class offering for charging, service, vehicles, batteries, and anything else that our clients need."

IUC is engaged with several opportunities in the United States and internationally where client hosts are seeking to upgrade charging infrastructure as well as deploy strategically adjacent assets that rely on or augement that infrastructure, including heavy- and light-use fleet vehicles, battery storage systems, and solar energy generation.

The LOI contemplates a staged review process during which the parties intend to exchange technical, commercial and diligence materials; assess potential vehicle fit, specifications, certifications, production capacity and delivery assumptions; evaluate local-market body builders, contract manufacturers and suppliers; develop service and support plans; and coordinate customer-facing proposals, subject in all respects to diligence, approvals and definitive agreements.

The LOI also contemplates the evaluation of a commercially viable pathway for GreenPower vehicle platforms to be completed, body-built or assembled locally in markets where IUC is expanding. Any such pathway would remain subject to engineering validation, homologation and certifications, import and customs treatment, local-content analysis, regulatory review, customer acceptance and definitive documentation.

For further information contact:

Fraser Atkinson, CEO

(604) 220-8048

Brendan Riley, President

(510) 910-3377

About GreenPower Motor Company Inc.GreenPower designs, builds and distributes a full suite of high-floor and low-floor all-electric medium and heavy-duty vehicles, including transit buses, school buses, shuttles, cargo van and a cab and chassis. GreenPower employs a clean-sheet design to manufacture all-electric vehicles that are purpose built to be battery powered with zero emissions while integrating global suppliers for key components. This OEM platform allows GreenPower to meet the specifications of various operators while providing standard parts for ease of maintenance and accessibility for warranty requirements. data.title: Caledonia Mining slides after cutting guidance for full-year production, raising cost outlook
data.description:
Caledonia Mining fell 2.6% in Friday's trading after reporting Q3 gold production at its Blanket mine in Zimbabwe declined 11% Y/Y to 19,106 oz, citing a shortage of compressed air at certain high-grade, high-volume mining areas and the temporary retention of gold within the processing circuit.

Caledonia said it expects production to normalize during Q4, as two of the new compressors have now been deployed and the last two have been released from the port and are being transported to the mine.

Due to the lower-than-expected production in Q3, Caledonia lowered Blanket production guidance for FY 2026 to a range of 69,000-72,500 oz from its previous outlook for 72,000-76,500 oz; the revised full-year guidance implies production at Blanket of 19,800-23,300 oz.

Reflecting the lower expected production volumes, the company also raised its full-year on-mine cost guidance to $1,700-$1,900/oz sold from a prior view $1,600-$1,800/oz sold, and hiked all-in sustaining cost guidance to $2,650-$2,850/oz sold from its earlier forecast of $2,500-$2,700/oz AISC.

"Although we have revised our guidance for 2026 to reflect the third-quarter performance, Blanket remains a robust and cash-generative operation," Caledonia CEO Mark Learmonth said.

data.title: Netflix Stocks Slip Lower as Skydance Debt Sharpens Valuation Debate
data.description:
Netflix , the global streaming and advertising company, slipped approximately 0.8% to $70.96 on Friday, October 9. The investment pitch is straightforward: a streaming business with fewer financial complications than rivals navigating major deals. According to Barron's, Netflix offers a simpler investment case than Skydance. The valuation picture puts its shares 31.17% below the $103.10 GF Value estimate, suggesting a potential discount rather than guaranteeing a rebound.

The earnings multiple adds another angle. Barron's put Netflix at roughly 18 times projected 2027 earnings and highlighted Deutsche Bank's upgrade to Buy from Hold, with a $95 price target. That leaves about 34% upside from Friday's price. The operating numbers provide some backing: second-quarter revenue rose 13% to $12.56 billion, while operating income climbed 11% to $4.19 billion. Revenue is growing. Profit needs to keep pace.

A cleaner corporate story helps, but Netflix still has to earn the rerating. Advertising must bring in more money. Programming spending must deliver enough engagement to justify the bill. With third-quarter results scheduled for October 20, the next test is close: can Netflix turn audience demand into faster earnings growth without letting content costs swallow the gains?

data.title: Nuinsco Announces Adoption of Semi-Annual Reporting
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Toronto – TheNewswire - October 9, 2026 – Nuinsco Resources Limited (“Nuinsco” or the “Company”) (CSE: NWI, FRA: NJX) today announced that it has elected to rely on Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers (the “Blanket Order”) and adopt semi-annual financial reporting, beginning with its third-quarter reporting period ended September 30, 2026.

    The Blanket Order permits eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from quarterly to semi-annual financial reporting by providing exemptions from the requirement to file interim financial reports and related management’s discussion and analysis (“MD&A”) for their first and third quarters.

    The Company has filed its interim financial reports and related MD&A for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and the six months ended June 30, 2026. Having now satisfied the eligibility requirements under the Blanket Order, the Company will first rely on the exemption for the nine-month interim period ended September 30, 2026. Accordingly, Nuinsco will not file an interim financial report or related MD&A for that period.

    Nuinsco’s financial year ends on December 31. Under the semi-annual reporting framework, the Company will continue to file:

    • Audited annual financial statements and related annual MDA within 120 days of its financial year-end; and


    • Six-month interim financial reports and related MDA within 60 days of June 30 each year.


    The Company’s next scheduled financial reporting will therefore be its audited annual financial statements and related MD&A for the year ending December 31, 2026.

    The Company intends to continue relying on the exemption for subsequent first- and third-quarter reporting periods, subject to its continued eligibility and the availability of the applicable exemptions. Adopting semi-annual reporting is intended to reduce reporting costs and administrative requirements, allowing management to devote additional resources to advancing the Company’s exploration and development activities.

    Nuinsco will continue to comply with its other continuous disclosure obligations, including timely disclosure of material changes and applicable Canadian Securities Exchange reporting requirements.

    This news release is being filed pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51 – 933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers.

    About Nuinsco Resources Limited

    Nuinsco Resources has more than 50 years of exploration suc­cess and is a growth-oriented, multi-commodity mineral explora­tion and development company focused on prospective oppor­tunities in Canada and internationally. Currently the Company has the large multi-commodity (phosphate, rare earth element, niobi­um, tantalum) Prairie Lake Project near Marathon-Terrace Bay, the Zig Zag Lake Property (lithium, tantalum) near Armstrong currently operated as a joint venture with First Class Metals PLC, the Paradise Lake gold project in central Newfoundland, and retains a NSR royalty on the Sunbeam Gold Property near Atikokan.

data.title: Corn futures plunge after USDA raises US yield outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Benchmark corn futures contract down as much as 30-cent daily trading limit
  • USDA lifts average corn yield outlook to 181.2 bushels per acre from 178.5
  • USDA raises US corn harvest forecast to 16.034 billion bushels from 15.800 billion
  • Soybeans fall to six-week low, wheat hits two-month low

By Karl Plume

US corn futures plunged by as much as the daily trading limit on Friday after the US Department of Agriculture shocked traders with an unexpected increase to its 2026 US harvest outlook.

Soybeans and wheat followed corn lower, pressured by the USDA's stock forecast increases for the two crops.

The USDA forecast the US corn harvest at 16.034 billion bushels, up from its outlook for 15.800 billion a month ago, with an average yield of 181.2 bushels per acre, up from 178.5 bpa previously. The revision swelled its end-of-season stocks outlook by 282 million bushels from a month earlier.

Analysts polled by Reuters, on average, expected production and average yield estimates to decrease following adverse crop weather this summer.

"To have USDA find the increased production this year was a shock. And in fact, as much as they did was a real big shock. So it was a negative report, obviously, and the market is reacting in a negative way," said Jack Scoville, analyst with The Price Group.

Benchmark Chicago Board of Trade December corn futures (CZ26) were down 29-1/2 cents at a two-month low of $4.70-3/4 per bushel at 11:50 a.m. CDT (1650 GMT) after sinking by as much as the daily 30-cent limit following the report. March futures (CH27) were also briefly limit-down.

November soybeans (SX26) were down 16-1/2 cents at $12.71 a bushel, a six-week low, while December wheat (WZ26) was down 19-3/4 cents at a two-month low of $6.63-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: JPMorgan Spots Stunning Shift in S&P 500
data.description:
Artificial intelligence has become so dominant in U.S. equities that a JPMorgan basket of just 41 AI-linked companies now represents 49% of the S&P 500's market value, underscoring how heavily the broader market increasingly depends on a single investment theme.

The concentration is historically unusual. JPMorgan noted that one industry has not commanded a comparable share of the U.S. stock market since railroads dominated equities in the nineteenth century. The same AI basket has also generated roughly two-thirds of the S&P 500's increase in market capitalization this year.

Nvidia is the basket's largest component at 8.21% of the S&P 500, followed by Apple at 7.05%, Alphabet at 6.13%, Microsoft at 5.65% and Amazon at 4.02%.

But this isn't simply another Magnificent Seven statistic.

JPMorgan's basket stretches across the AI supply chain, including Broadcom (AVGO), Micron , Advanced Micro Devices , Oracle , Palantir , Arista Networks , Eaton , Constellation Energy and data-center power beneficiaries such as Vistra .

That breadth helps explain why AI has increasingly become a market-level factor rather than merely a technology-sector trade.

The concentration is showing up elsewhere. The 10 largest S&P 500 companies now account for roughly 40% of the index, while Reuters noted this week that AI and technology exposure has pushed broader market concentration beyond levels seen during the dot-com era.

Investor Takeaway

For investors holding S&P 500 funds such as SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) or iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV), this matters because owning the index no longer necessarily means having balanced exposure across competing economic themes.

Nearly half of every market-cap-weighted dollar is now indirectly tied to JPMorgan's AI complex.

That concentration has been extremely rewarding while AI earnings and spending have accelerated. Technology companies are expected to account for roughly two-thirds of S&P 500 earnings growth in the third quarter, according to current estimates.

But concentration works both ways. If AI earnings, capital spending or valuations disappoint, weakness across a relatively small group of companies could have an unusually large effect on the entire index.

For investors, the number to watch is therefore no longer simply Nvidia's growth rate. It is whether earnings growth across the rest of the S&P 500 begins catching up with the companies currently carrying nearly half the market.

data.title: Delta Airlines Stock Faces New Pressure After Major Outlook Reset
data.description:
Delta Air Lines (DAL) shares fell about 5% in premarket trading Friday after the carrier missed September-quarter expectations and cut its full-year profit outlook as sharply higher fuel costs squeezed margins.

The airline reported adjusted earnings of $1.72 per share, while operating margin fell to 9.4% from 11.1% a year earlier. Delta now expects full-year adjusted earnings of $5.10 to $5.60 per share, down from its previous forecast of $6.50 to $7.50.

That is a meaningful reset.

Reuters reported that Delta is dealing with roughly $6 billion of additional fuel expense, driven by higher crude and refined jet-fuel prices. The airline has managed to raise fares by about 25% year over year, but those increases have not fully offset the surge in energy costs.

The company's own refinery is providing some cushion. Delta expects its Monroe refinery near Philadelphia to generate roughly $700 million of profit in 2026, partially offsetting the fuel shock.

Demand itself remains comparatively healthy.

Management continues to point to strong travel trends, but the problem is increasingly one of economics: pushing ticket prices much higher risks damaging demand, while absorbing higher fuel costs directly pressures margins.

For the December quarter, Delta expects adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.65, another indication that the cost environment remains difficult.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important takeaway is that Delta's problem is not weak demand. It is the cost of serving that demand.

That distinction matters.

If travel demand were collapsing, investors would be dealing with a much more fundamental revenue problem. Instead, Delta is seeing strong pricing and passenger demand, but fuel costs are rising faster than the company can pass them through.

That makes oil and jet-fuel prices the most important near-term variables for Delta investors.

The broader airline industry faces the same pressure. Elevated jet-fuel prices are forcing carriers to consider higher fares and could continue squeezing margins well into 2027 if energy markets remain tight.

For Delta, I would watch fuel expense, operating margin, fare growth and whether the company can stabilize its earnings outlook without weakening passenger demand.

If fuel prices ease, earnings leverage could improve quickly. If they stay elevated, even strong travel demand may not be enough to protect margins.

data.title: Nvidia Is Opening the Door to Rival Chips
data.description:
The leading provider of AI accelerators, Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials), is supporting a company creating what at first glance might seem strange: infrastructure intended to enable competing AI processors to cooperate.

Token Fabric, a hardware and software networking framework intended to link several AI processor types within a single data center, was introduced by Upscale AI on Thursday.

The system combines hardware driven by Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet technology with networking chips made by Upscale. Software keeps an eye out for equipment issues and network constraints.

The objective is simple. Expensive AI computers only produce returns while they are operating, and sluggish data transfer between chips may result in idle processing power.

Barun Kar, CEO of Upscale, anticipates that Token Fabric will make tens of millions of dollars in revenue the next year, possibly as much as hundreds of millions. After receiving an additional $190 million, the startup's valuation reached $2 billion in June, bringing its total investment to over $500 million.

Investors in Nvidia find the plan to be more intriguing.

GPUs and bespoke accelerators from various manufacturers are becoming more and more important to cloud providers. Nvidia may gain from mixed-chip systems utilizing its networking capabilities rather than relying just on consumers adopting Nvidia chips everywhere.

As a result, networking offers Nvidia an additional means of staying integrated into the AI infrastructure stack despite growing processor competition.

It is anticipated that the initial part of Token Fabric will be released in the fourth quarter, with a more extensive deployment continuing until 2027.

data.title: Cable One plunges on report lender filed lawsuit to block Mega Broadband deal
data.description:
Cable One cratered 35% after a report that a lender filed a lawsuit seeking to block the cable operator from purchasing a 55% equity stake in Mega Broadband from financial sponsor GTCR.

CoBank, which says it holds about $1.1 billion in secured credit issued by Cable One , asked a federal judge in New York to issue an emergency restraining order to prevent the company from transferring about $480 million for the Mega Broadband purchase, according a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited the lawsuit.

Cable One faces a Friday deadline to complete the purchase.

The lender said the transfer of funds would make Cable One “sink deeper into insolvency and make its remaining assets unreasonably small given its already large debts.”

Representatives for Cable One, CoBank and GTCR didn’t immediately respond to Bloomberg requests for comment.

data.title: Warner Bros. Has Never Been the Answer to Anyone's Problems — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Major technological shifts, from the dot-com boom to artificial intelligence, have long rattled the media business.

Over the years, many legacy media companies have adapted to a quickly changing landscape by doing the same thing: trying to get bigger.

The result has been a series of Frankenstein-like "monsters," or mergers that have inevitably collapsed as grand theories have collided with reality, Barclays wrote in a note Friday.

Analyst Kannan Venkateshwar said legacy media companies have repeatedly attempted to address technology-driven shifts by acquiring content scale, mistakenly viewing new technologies merely as cheaper distribution channels for existing products.

He analyzed Warner Bros., which he sees as a key example for these attempts.

Warner Bros. has had a long history of high-profile and volatile mergers. The motivation was simple: create a dominant media empire. What transpired instead were collapses due to poor timing, intense cultural clashes, and strategic miscalculations, he wrote. Each merger was meant to navigate a shifting media landscape, yet each attempt misread where the competitive leverage actually lay.

At the height of the dot-com boom, America Online, known as AOL, bought Time Warner as a way to pair an expiring dial-up gateway with legacy content, assuming the internet would work like digital cable. But the dot-com crash ended up wiping out AOL's stock value and dial-up internet collapsed as broadband rose.

Almost two decades later, telecommunications giant AT&T acquired Time Warner for about $85 billion, renaming the entertainment arm WarnerMedia. AT&T tried to leverage studio content to sell its mobile data plans, but the venture collapsed.

Venkateshwar noted the deal failed to recognize that Netflix's advantage was its software and ease of discovery, not its pipe ownership. The deal's high debt also restricted necessary transition investments, he noted.

In 2022, AT&T gave up on those entertainment ambitions, spinning off WarnerMedia to merge with Discovery Inc. in a $43 billion transaction, creating Warner Bros. Discovery, led by David Zaslav. But trouble loomed: the company inherited the decline of cable TV and high debt, pushing Warner Bros. to pursue corporate restructurings and studio asset sales.

The recent merger with Paramount, which finalized earlier this week to create Skydance, has only added to the pile of repeated mistakes, Venkateshwar noted. He said the deal expands content scale at a time when artificial intelligence has shifted value toward conversational interfaces, agents, and personalized experiences.

"Today most closely resembles 2000 as the direction of travel is clear, but the winning architecture is not," Venkateshwar wrote Friday.

Instead of opting for megamergers, Venkateshwar advised legacy media companies to adopt three primary strategies.

First, he recommended that businesses invest in future technologies without taking on massive financial risk. He pointed to Disney's recent investment in Epic Games and Webtoon, which veered away from a potential acquisition.

The analyst added that companies should move away from isolated streaming catalogs by licensing intellectual property through clear permissions and revenue sharing to let external developers make stories interactive.

Lastly, Venkateshwar wrote that legacy media companies should focus on how content is found and personalized through AI rather than simply creating more shows. Ownership of this user interface, he believes, could grant far more leverage than raw catalog size.

Write to Mariapaula Gonzalez at mariapaula.gonzalez@barrons.com
